_doc: Tier-B treks (generated by tools/trails/osm_tail.py from OpenStreetMap, ODbL, and the Copernicus DEM; never edit by hand).

trails.name: Rakiura - north west circuit
trails.why: Allow 9–11 days to walk the full 125 km circuit. This track is suitable for fit, well equipped and experienced trampers.

trails.name: Travers-Sabine Circuit
trails.why: The Travers-Sabine Circuit is a popular tramping route in Nelson Lakes National Park, New Zealand.

trails.name: Te Ara Hura
trails.why: Collection of walks to explore Waiheke Island and discover its natural beauty. On Te Ara Hura walking track network you can explore the coastline, pass through native bush and visit historic sites.

trails.name: TAR - Schorman-Kaitoke main range traverse
trails.why: Traverses 35 named peaks and includes around 6800m of vertical gain. A large majority of the route is in the sub-alpine zone, so is subject to very changeable weather.

trails.name: Wangapeka Track
trails.why: The Wangapeka Track is a tramping track in the north-west of the South Island of New Zealand.

trails.name: Saint James Walkway
trails.why: The St James Walkway is a 66 kilometres-long subalpine tramping track located in the Lewis Pass area of the South Island of New Zealand.

trails.name: Te Awa River Walk
trails.why: Te Awa, caters to people of all ages and abilities and was designed for both cyclists and pedestrians.

trails.name: Te Araroa - alternative Drury to Rangariri
trails.why: This alternative route avoids walking SH1 and SH2 after Bombay, and unformed paths Mercer and Meremere Shows flat farming country at its best.

trails.name: The Three Passes
trails.why: This classic summer tramp for experienced backcountry trampers crosses Harman Pass, Whitehorn Pass and Browning Pass/Noti Raureka.

trails.name: Te Paki Coastal Track
trails.why: This stunning coastal track offers spectacular views of our northern coastline, regenerating bush and large wind-swept sand dunes.

trails.name: Te Araroa - 10 Otago - alt
trails.why: Te Araroa is New Zealand's long distance tramping route, stretching circa 3,000 kilometres along the length of the country's two main islands from Cape Reinga to Bluff.

trails.name: Arahua and Styx Valleys Tracks
trails.why: The Arahura and Styx valleys are popular areas for tramping and hunting. The main access in both valleys is via benched formations constructed during the early gold mining days.

trails.name: TAR - northern crossing
trails.why: Northern Crossing links the Ōhau and Waingawa catchments in Tararua Forest Park - one of four classic tramps here - 3 to 5 days - expert route

trails.name: TAR - southern crossing
trails.why: 1 of 4 classics links Otaki and Tauherenikau catchments. Originally from Otaki Forks to Wairarapa Plains and now the Kaitoke Basin.

trails.name: Hutt River Trail
trails.why: Hutt River Trail runs from Petone Station along the beachfront to Hikoikoi Reserve and from there to Te Marua, Upper Hutt where it links into the Remutaka Rail Trail.

trails.name: Dun Mountain Trail - walking
trails.why: Dun Mountain Trail follows New Zealand’s first railway bringing minerals from Wooded Peak.

trails.name: Historic Haast to Paringa Cattle Track
trails.why: This track was built in 1875 by farmers at Haast. Stock were driven from the Landsborough and Cascade valleys to sale yards at Whataroa.

trails.name: Te Ara Pātaka
trails.why: Enjoy magnificent views over Banks Peninsula, the Canterbury plains, Southern Alps and Pacific Ocean on this track, which is about an hour's drive from Christchurch.

trails.name: Hutt River Trail west
trails.why: Hutt River Trail west follows the right bank of Te Awa Kairangi from the mouth to Birchville.

trails.name: Aotea Track
trails.why: The Aotea Track offers a range of spectacular landscapes, superb views and rich history.

trails.name: Silverpeaks Circuit Track
trails.why: Silverpeaks Circuit Track provides a challenging tramp through the Silverpeaks Scenic Reserve.

trails.name: Waipapa River Track
trails.why: This scenic two-day tramp follows the Waipapa River through the heart of Puketī Forest. It is only recommended for experienced and well-equipped trampers.

trails.name: Gibbs Hill
trails.why: The Gibbs Hill Track crosses Abel Tasman National Park inland between Wainui and Tōtaranui.

trails.name: Puke Ariki
trails.why: " 7 to 8 Hours one way This day trip traverses the valleys and ridge tops of the eastern side of the park.

trails.name: Inland Pack Track
trails.why: The Inland Pack Track is a trail in the Paparoa National Park on West Coast of New Zealand.

trails.name: Skyline Walkway
trails.why: This track runs from Johnsonville south west to Makara Saddle, Karori. Allow up to 5 hours to traverse 12kms of Wellington’s ridge tops following the Outer Green Belt

trails.name: Mt Holdsworth - Jumbo Circuit
trails.why: The classic Mt Holdsworth - Jumbo Circuit is a 2 to 3 day tramp involving a climb through beech-podocarp forest to some of the best alpine tops travel in the Tararua Forest Park.

trails.name: Holdsworth - Kaitoke extension
trails.why: walking route from Masterton to start of Holdsworth - Kaitoke Track

trails.name: Coast to Coast Walkway (Waitematā to Manukau)
trails.why: In three stages you walk through landscapes shaped by 600 years of Māori occupation, and through some of our finest natural and built heritage areas offering panoramic views along the way.

trails.name: Coast to Coast Walkway (Manukau to Waitematā)
trails.why: In three stages you walk through landscapes shaped by 600 years of Māori occupation, and through some of our finest natural and built heritage areas offering panoramic views along the way.

trails.name: Burttons Track
trails.why: Burtton's Track lies between Palmerston North and Shannon.

trails.name: Carrington Hut Route
trails.why: This route up the braided riverbed of the Waimakariri leads to a comfortable hut situated below the park’s highest peaks.

trails.name: Te Ara Moana - SH88 section of Te Aka Ōtākou
trails.why: The trail from Port Chalmers to beyond Portobello is named Te Aka Ōtākou, the winding path clinging to the harbour.

trails.name: Kokowai Track Round Trip
trails.why: A great all day hike for those wanting both an alpine and forest experience.

trails.name: Wind turbine to Red Rocks
trails.why:
From Wind Turbine car park follow marked trails: 
Windmill to Carparts Ext. 
Then right to Barking Emu
Then Red Rocks along ridges until you
get down to the coast. 
Return to Owhiro Bay via Red Rocks Coastal Walk. 
Exposed

trails.name: Coastal Walkway
trails.why: The Coastal Walkway is a 12.7-kilometre long walkway located along the coast of New Plymouth, New Zealand.

trails.name: Southern Walkway
trails.why: 11 km walk between Oriental Bay and Island Bay: 4–5 hours. Steep in places, not difficult overall: average fitness.

trails.name: Mount Arthur
trails.why: Located in the northwest corner of New Zealand's South Island, Kahurangi is New Zealand's second largest national park.

trails.name: Manawatū Gorge Track
trails.why: Walk through native bush, enjoy scenic views and experience native wildlife only a short distance from Palmerston North.

trails.name: Burttons Track access
trails.why: an extension to show access to Burttons Track - from the south east end of Fitzherbert Avenue, Palmerston North to the south end of Scotts Road and the start of Burttons Track.

trails.name: Waikanae River Loop
trails.why: With the estuary, a nationally significant area. Birds use it to travel between the Tararua’s and Kapiti.

trails.name: Careys Creek Track
trails.why: Careys Creek Track is a tramping track about 20 km north of Dunedin, in the South Island of New Zealand.

trails.name: Belmont Trig Loop
trails.why: GWRC says\n\nAn energetic round trip, taking in panoramic views from the highest point in the park, along with native forest in the middle part of Korokoro Valley

trails.name: Hutt Road shared path - Wellington to Petone
trails.region: assumed Wellington City Council from Aotea Quay to Ngauranga and NZTA (for SH2) on to Petone
trails.why: Between 2016 and 2018 the 1.4 km section from Aotea Quay to Rangiora Avenue was significantly upgraded, including new surfaces and elimination of casual car parking

trails.name: Pearl Harbour to Hope Arm Track
trails.why: The track leads through beech forest to a very pleasant bay on Lake Manapouri, with a great swimming spot and hut.

trails.name: Hutt Road shared path - Wellington to Johnsonville
trails.region: Wellington City Council from Wellington Station to Ngauranga and NZTA on to Johnsonville as part of
trails.why: Between 2016 and 2018 the 1.4 km section from Aotea Quay to Rangiora Avenue was significantly upgraded, including new surfaces and elimination of casual car parking

trails.name: Sanctuary to Sea
trails.why: The Kaiwharawhara Stream is a large system with habitat for short jaw, banded and giant kōkopu and kōaro The route passes through Otari Bush, Churchill Drive and Trelissick Park to the Hutt Road and the entrance to the sea at Te Whanganui-a-Tara.

trails.name: Fenceline
trails.why: Follow the boundary of the Zealandia Te Māra a Tāne ecosanctuary and tune into native birdsong.

trails.name: Tahurangi Translator Tower Round Trip
trails.why: A scenic climb to a viewing point beside a commercial translator tower. This track travels into the alpine environment and may be impassable due to snow and ice in the winter.

trails.name: Pearl Harbour Circle Track
trails.why: This tramping track takes you on a pleasant, half-day walk through beech forest near Manapouri, to a hill viewpoint overlooking the lake.

trails.name: Mangaone Walkway
trails.why: Old bush tramway in low hill country east of Waikanae\nNorth: crosses farmland\nSouth: Waikanae River and Kaitawa Scenic Reserve protecting previously milled podocarp forest.

trails.name: Waimapihi Reserve Loop Walk
trails.why: Starts near the Aro Street bus terminus the path wends south and west up to Polhill. The descent, skirting the Zealandia fence line, is to George Denton Park then to Holloway Road and back to Aro Street.

trails.name: Pearl Harbour to Back Valley Hut Track
trails.why: A tramping track leading through beech forest to Back Valley Hut near Manapouri, with a side trip option to peaceful Lake Rakatu.

trails.name: Rangituhi Walk
trails.why: Climb to the summit of this 468 m peak for views on a clear day from the Inland Kaikoura Range to Taranaki; a good option for older children.

trails.name: Te Araroa - extreme weather alternative from Camp Elsdon, Porirua
trails.why: an alternative in extreme weather to avoid being on an the exposed top of Rangituhi

trails.name: Langsview Track
trails.why: For amazing views of the countryside and coastline, follow this track along the ridgeline of the Brynderwyn range.

trails.name: Mākara Walkway
trails.why: This loop walk climbs to vantage points with spectacular views - farmland, a beach and gun emplacements will keep kids interested.

trails.name: TAR - Smith Creek
trails.why: This is a daytrip in the southern Tararua Range and the exit/entry to the Kaitoke-Holdsworth Tramp.

trails.name: Maketawa Hut Circuit
trails.why: This is a good day or overnight tramp, with fantastic views of Taranaki Maunga from Maketawa Hut.

trails.name: Mangorei Track to Pouākai Tarns
trails.why: On a fine day enjoy spectacular views of Taranaki and the Pouākai tarns on this day hike or overnight tramp.

trails.name: York Road Loop Track
trails.why: Explore the remnants of the old Egmont Branch railway quarry complex while walking through native forest.

trails.name: Mount Climie Track
trails.why: The Mt Climie ridge provides the southern and eastern backdrop to Upper Hutt. It is also part of the long northern skyline of the Remutaka Range seen across the harbour from Wellington City.

trails.name: Gentle Annie
trails.why: One of the most popular day trips in the park is the climb to Mountain House Shelter along the easy grade of the Gentle Annie Track.

trails.name: Mount Te Kinga Track/Ara O Te Kinga
trails.why: Climb to a lookout for spectacular views, or continue to the summit of Mount Te Kinga.

trails.name: Bothamley (shared) pathway
trails.why: Running alongside the Kenepuru Stream, this pathway is on its way to become the ‘green heart of Porirua’ thanks to an environment development programme.

trails.name: Pupū Hydro Walkway
trails.why: Retracing an old gold-mining water race, this short walk passes through forest of young beech and rimu to mature podocarps - it's good for children but be sure to supervise them.

trails.name: Wairakau Stream Track
trails.why: After the track road out of Totara North, the trail is T2 with roots and rutted sections; on the approach to Kairara Rock / Dukes Nose, there are two pitches that are secured with metal poles that require scrambling and are T3 classification

trails.name: Te Ara Utiwai
trails.why: From Elsdon Camp for about 6 km towards Rangituhi to 350 m asl. A further path continues to the top of Rangituhi.

trails.name: Te Araroa alternative route near Auckland
trails.why: Alternative to avoid 1) rahui at Okura Bush Walkway to assist Kauri die back issue and 2) low tide alternatives.

trails.name: Puketiro Loop - Up
trails.why: Also bridleway for horses. After MWay, take left hand side up. Warm clothing: strong winds on the tops.

trails.name: Puketiro Loop - Down
trails.why:
Also bridleway for horses.
From top continue down left side.
Warm clothing: strong winds on the tops.
Track climbs steeply through pines.
Great views of Pauatahanui Inlet: and South Island on a clear day.

trails.name: Mount Iron Loop
trails.why: This very popular loop walk offers excellent 360-degree views from the summit.

trails.name: Roberts Point
trails.why: Roberts Point Track is an 11–12.3-kilometre tramping track in Franz Josef Glacier and Westland Tai Poutini National Park, New Zealand.

trails.name: Te Araroa - 10 Otago - facilities
trails.why: Te Araroa is New Zealand's long distance tramping route, stretching circa 3,000 kilometres along the length of the country's two main islands from Cape Reinga to Bluff.

trails.name: Bridle Path
trails.why: 1850: Canterbury's first European settlers from Lyttelton to Christchurch. Steep track. Stunning views from city to the Southern Alps and Lyttelton and Banks Peninsula.

trails.name: Korokoro Valley Walk
trails.why: GWRC says\n\nA graded track follows the old water pipeline up to the historic Korokoro Dam.

trails.name: Fanthams Peak / Panitahi and Syme Hut Track
trails.why: From December to April, fit and well-equipped trampers can enjoy spectacular scenery from Panitahi, formerly known as Fanthams Peak, on Taranaki Maunga.
